swap_risks: HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 13x (OPA2134UA: 5 pA p.7 vs TL072IDR: 65 pA p.15); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 2.9x (OPA2134UA: 4000 µA/ch p.8 vs TL072IDR: 1400 µA/ch p.16); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: OPA2134UA requires Vs,min >= 5 V (p.5) vs 4.5 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.
engineering_verdict: OPA2134UA (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and TL072IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because input bias current Ib differs 13x (CMOS vs bipolar input stage); quiescent supply current Iq/ch differs 2.9x; Vs,min floor rises 0.5 V. Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 8 MHz (p.7) vs 5.25 MHz (p.15), supply ceiling 36 V (p.5) vs 40 V (p.11), Vos 3.5 mV (p.7) vs 6 mV (p.15), Ib 13x gap (5 vs 65 pA), voltage noise 8 vs 37 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: OPA2134UA "High 4 mA/ch Quiescent Current Causes 38°C–48°C Self-Heating in SOIC-8 at ±15 V" (p.8) and TL072IDR "Negative-Rail Input Headroom Limit and Legacy Phase Reversal Trap" (p.11). BOM decision: Choose OPA2134UA when closed-loop signal bandwidth requires 8 MHz GBWP or high-impedance sensors require pA-class input bias (5 pA); choose TL072IDR when ultra-low supply current (1400 µA/ch) is prioritized. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.5) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
